purpose: Whole-home, fleet-aware local energy planning recommendation using vehicle SoC, home energy history, optional home battery, and persisted user assumptions.
primaryGoal: Compare readiness, cost, solar self-consumption, grid peaks and constraints, adjust assumptions, and download the complete recommendation without commanding any device.

dataSources.name: Account vehicles
dataSources.sourceOwnership: Shared vehicle query; account fleet, not a header-selected single vehicle.
dataSources.behavior: Composition uses data ?? []; vehicles supply identity, names and list SoC fallback. Backend response correctness is unverified.

dataSources.name: Fleet live state
dataSources.sourceOwnership: Shared vehicle live-query owner; batch observations and retained readings remain distinct from query completion time.
dataSources.behavior: Nonempty fleet enables request; cancellation signal is forwarded, live cache policy retained, failed entries may retain observations. Composition reports oldest observed timestamp, failed and retained counts instead of wrapper success freshness.

dataSources.name: Home energy site discovery
dataSources.sourceOwnership: Shared Tesla home-energy query; separate from vehicle energy endpoints.
dataSources.behavior: Select first battery/solar-capable site, otherwise first site. No page site picker; preserve this selection rather than introducing a new workspace filter.

dataSources.name: Selected home site information
dataSources.sourceOwnership: Shared home energy query; present in freshness/source notices, not used to derive actual tariff or model battery specification.
dataSources.behavior: Enabled only with site ID; slow stale-time policy and cancellation retained.

dataSources.name: Home battery SoC
dataSources.sourceOwnership: Shared home energy live status; not vehicle battery state.
dataSources.behavior: Only used when scenario battery is enabled; live percentage_charged precedes site percentage_charged, then a disclosed 50% model assumption.

dataSources.name: Solar and household load history
dataSources.sourceOwnership: Shared home energy history query, consumed by two separate pure forecast adapters.
dataSources.behavior: No since/until supplied here: day history informs future scenario horizon, not a workspace historical range. Frontend expects interval Wh and derives W using next sample gap or a five-minute fallback, UTC day-shape and nearest sampled slot filling. Missing history yields modeled zero series with confidence 0 / quality none, not measured zero. Backend parser/actual history unit and coverage not inspected or proven.

dataSources.name: Persisted assumptions and local optimizer
dataSources.sourceOwnership: Feature-owned localStorage and pure computation; not server state or a device control API.
dataSources.behavior: Preserve teslasync:home-energy-orchestrator:scenario:v1, sanitizers, cross-tab storage subscriptions and in-memory fallback. W/Wh inputs and outputs remain raw; percent, ISO instants, slotMinutes and deliberate currency-per-kWh tariff representation remain unchanged. Optimizer implementation and algorithm correctness were not audited.

visualIssues.detail: ProgressRing hard-codes emerald/amber hex; unmet caption at line 66 forces text-amber-300, and violation icons separately force emerald/red/amber shades. These ignore effective theme contrast and shared severity tokens.

architectureIssues.detail: loadForecastW comment says household base load excludes vehicle charging, whereas forecastAdapters.ts:29-32 explicitly says Gateway household history may already include charging and cannot be decomposed. This is a source-documentation inconsistency, not proof of a backend or optimizer defect.
architectureIssues.fix: Retain the source caveat in user-facing assumptions; reconcile documentation under a separate scoped change without subtracting invented vehicle load or altering raw data.

dataBehavior: Keep the separate vehicle fleet and home energy site sources. Do not replace home solar/load history with vehicle energy telemetry or assume site ownership from selected vehicle.

Vehicle SoC precedence: finite fleet battery_level, finite list battery_level/batteryLevel, then disclosed 50% model assumption. Battery precedence: live site SoC, discovery site SoC, then 50% when battery scenario enabled.
Preserve separate solar/load history confidence, sample count and latest timestamp; confidence is not source trust or vehicle readiness confidence.

Keep raw W/Wh in computation/export/cache; user preferences applied only at presentation. Existing currency-per-kWh tariff representation and slotMinutes are deliberate domain contracts, not a migration opportunity.
Preserve UTC tariff/departure/day-shape semantics, future horizon start/end-exclusive, default 15-minute slots/24-hour horizon, optional battery off by default, and forecast approximations.
Preserve six KPIs: overall score, projected net cost, self-consumption, peak import, ready/total vehicles and unmet Wh.

Preserve six energy flow series and sign conventions: battery positive charge/negative discharge, grid export rendered negative; chart data rounded at display preparation, canonical JSON keeps exact input/result.
All ten section calls remain mounted during source degradation. Conditional battery/deadline controls and optional heatmap row are legitimate business conditions, not global data gates.
No autonomous command, tariff fetch capability, actual site limits or measured battery specification may be invented.
